$doc: The head of an inner page, in the order the owner approved: a kicker that names WHOSE page this is, a title, a lede, and a slot for the tags that follow. Every value here is transcribed from `.mcp-head`, which is the one place the pattern existed and is the measurement it was approved against — kicker to title is `space-flow-sm` (20px at an 800px-tall window), title to lede is `space-4`, and the lede's bottom margin meets the meta's top margin at `space-5` and collapses to one 20px gap. The kicker's accent underline is the pattern's signature, and is why the kicker is inline-block rather than a block: the rule has to be the width of the words, not the width of the column.

block.title: Page head
note: The head an inner page opens with — the five work pages and /mcp. It goes on the
BAND rather than inside the well, because the one rule it makes about the page's
geometry is a rule about the well: an inner page's head is the thing that has to
clear the floating bar, and the clearance REPLACES the well's own top padding
rather than adding to it. Everything else is the four parts, in order.

rules.name: well
rules.$doc: The nav clearance, and the one rule this component makes about somebody else's element. `--space-nav` replaces the well's own `--pad-y` rather than adding to it, which is why it is a padding on the well and not a margin on anything inside it; and it prints as nothing, because `--space-nav`'s print value is 0 and `.bar` is not on the sheet.

rules.name: kicker
rules.$doc: Whose page this is — a client name on a work page, the protocol's name on /mcp. `inline-block` so the accent rule under it is the width of the words rather than of the column, which is the whole reason it reads as a signature instead of a divider.

rules.name: title
rules.$doc: The page's one display line. The SIZE is not here: the title wears `t-display t-display--lg` from the type layer, because a typographic level is a utility applied to whatever element a page already has, and this component has no opinion about which heading it is.

rules.name: lede
rules.$doc: One paragraph, measured rather than sized. `46rem` is the measure /mcp's prose and its tool table already hold; a measure is a different job from spacing, which is why it is a literal here and on the owner's review list rather than a token.

rules.name: meta
rules.$doc: The slot the tags land in — chips on a work page, and nothing at all on /mcp, whose prose and link grid follow the head rather than sit in it. Its top margin is the same step as the lede's bottom margin ON PURPOSE: adjacent siblings collapse, so the pair is one 20px gap when both are present, and 20px above the meta when there is no lede.
